candidates.name: The Ram Folk Club
candidates.extract: The Ram Folk Club was a folk club in the borough of Elmbridge in suburban north Surrey, one of only a few folk clubs in the Home Counties close to London. Established in October 1983, it operated on Friday evenings and featured music by folk and acoustic artists and bands.

candidates.name: Metropolitan Police Sports Club Ground, East Molesey
candidates.extract: Metropolitan Police Sports Club Ground (also known as Imber Court) is a cricket ground in East Molesey, Surrey. The first recorded match on the ground was in 1940, when the Metropolitan Police played a British Empire XI.

candidates.name: Weston Green
candidates.extract: Weston Green is a small suburban village and a ward in the Elmbridge borough of Surrey. This area was, until 1901, a part of Thames Ditton with which it remains contiguous and associated.

candidates.name: Three Rivers Academy, Surrey
candidates.extract: Three Rivers Academy is a mixed, secondary school situated on Hersham Road, between Hersham and Walton-on-Thames in Surrey, England. The school has been awarded Specialist Business and Enterprise College status.

candidates.name: Ashley Park, Surrey
candidates.description: Private neighborhood in Walton-on-Thames, Surrey, UK
candidates.extract: Ashley Park is a private residential neighbourhood at Walton-on-Thames in Surrey. Its central feature was a grandiose English country house, at times enjoying associated medieval manorial rights, which stood on the site, with alterations, between 1605 and the early 1920s.

candidates.name: Molesey Road
candidates.description: Rugby union stadium in Hersham, England
candidates.extract: Molesey Road Stadium is a rugby union stadium in Hersham, Surrey, that is home to Esher RFC. The stadium contains a 1,200 seater main stand to the west of the pitch and a clubhouse in the south-east corner.

candidates.name: Hundred of Elmbridge
candidates.extract: The Hundred of Elmbridge or Elmbridge/Emley Hundred was a geographic subdivision (called a "hundred") in the north of the county of Surrey, England. The majority of its area forms the modern Borough of Elmbridge, with the remainder forming part of the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames in Greater London.

candidates.name: Stompond Lane Sports Ground
candidates.extract: The Sports Ground, Stompond Lane (also called Stompond Lane Sports Ground, but often just shortened to Stompond Lane) was a stadium located in Walton-on-Thames, Surrey. It was where Walton & Hersham F.C. played their home matches and it was also used by the Walton Athletic Club.

candidates.name: Hersham
candidates.extract: Hersham is a suburban village in Surrey, within the M25 and the Greater London Built-up Area. It has a mixture of low and high rise housing and has four technology/trading estates.

candidates.name: Walton-on-Thames railway station
candidates.extract: Walton-on-Thames railway station is at the southern edge of the town of Walton-on-Thames in Surrey, England and borders Burwood Park, Hersham. It is 17 mi from and is situated between and .

candidates.name: Esher and Walton
candidates.extract: Esher and Walton ( is a constituency in Surrey represented in the House of Commons of the UK Parliament. Since 2024, it has been represented by Monica Harding of the Liberal Democrats.

candidates.name: Hersham railway station
candidates.extract: Opened on 28 September 1936, Hersham railway station is on the London to Woking line and operated by South Western Railway. The station is 0.7 mi north of Hersham village centre, adjoined to one side by housing and the other by fields and a golf course.

candidates.name: Weybridge
candidates.extract: Weybridge is a town in the Borough of Elmbridge in Surrey, England, around 27 km south-west of central London. The settlement is recorded as Waigebrugge and Weibrugge in the 7th century and the name derives from a crossing point of the River Wey, which flows into the River Thames to the north of the town centre.

candidates.name: Weybridge United Reformed Church
candidates.extract: The Weybridge United Reformed Church (formerly Weybridge Congregational Church) situated at Queen's Road (the A 317 Road), Weybridge, near to its junction with York Road, is a Victorian Grade II Listed church building (or former church building) that is now used by the St.John's Mar Thoma church congregation, formerly being unused for worship.

candidates.name: North West Surrey Synagogue
candidates.extract: The North West Surrey Synagogue is a Reform Jewish congregation and synagogue, located on Oatlands Drive in Weybridge, Surrey, England, in the United Kingdom. The community was founded in 1968, and was a member of the Movement for Reform Judaism.

candidates.name: Heathside School
candidates.extract: Heathside School is a co-educational secondary school for students aged 11–18 situated in Brooklands Lane, Weybridge, Surrey, England. The Executive Principal is Anne Cullum.

candidates.name: Martin Hotine
candidates.extract: Brigadier Martin Hotine CMG CBE (17 June 1898 – 12 November 1968) was the head of the Trigonometrical and Levelling Division of the Ordnance Survey responsible for the 26-year-long retriangulation of Great Britain (1936–1962) and was the first Director General of the Directorate of Overseas Surveys (1946–1955).

candidates.name: BAC Concorde G-BBDG
candidates.description: First British production test supersonic airliner
candidates.extract: G-BBDG, known as "Delta Golf", is the British development Concorde built for evaluation testing. Along with the French Concorde F-WTSB, the aircraft was used to enable sufficient testing to allow for the Concorde fleet to receive certification.
